newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower on rains, spillover.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower on rains, spillover.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled lower on forecasts for crop-enhancing rains in North Dakota and on spillover pressure from CBOT wheat, traders said.
Spring wheat defied opening calls by starting lower on the day as Cargill Investor Services offered a 500,000-bushel chunk of September wheat for sale.
"That was a real shocker -- We had been expecting the market to open higher," a trader said. "I think (Cargill's selling) was a function of the recent rains and the forecasts for more this week."
Further pressure came as CBOT wheat weakened on harvesting, and as CBOT soybeans posted sharp losses amid speculative liquidation in the July contract.
MGE spring wheat settled 1/4 to 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with July down two cents at $3.82-3/4. New crop September was down 3-1/2 cents at $3.71.
Traders estimated Cargill Investor Services sold two million Sept bushels -- most of it before 11:00 a.m. CDT.
The MGE estimated Wednesday's spring wheat futures volume at 22.985 million bushels.
